requirement: A context preview is candidate-only: it carries no run id and no injection claim, and the request rejects a run_id parameter.
why_it_matters: backend-v1.4.md §5.4. A preview shows what WOULD be assembled. If it could carry the current session's run id, the same payload would be indistinguishable from a record of context actually served to that run — and the adapter would be one careless field away from forging an injection audit trail. The defence is doubled: the request refuses run_id, and the response model has no place to put one.

counterexamples.why: Exactly the accident the rule exists to prevent: an adapter that had the current run in hand and passed it through. The payload would now look like a record of context served to run_8fc21a, in a shape that creates no audit entry — an injection claim with nothing behind it.

counterexamples.name: a preview that dropped its candidate flag
counterexamples.why: candidate_only is const true. A preview that says it is not a candidate is asserting the context was really assembled and delivered, which this route never does.

counterexamples.name: an injection record claiming the model used the context
counterexamples.why: The platform can observe that it served context. It cannot observe that a model read or acted on it. A UI showing 'the agent used this lesson' on that basis would be reporting an inference as a measurement.
